history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration assign the responsibility of Chief Risk Officer to an existing senior executive in each entity, at the department, missions and service centres levels.
history.administration_response: A draft review of enterprise risk management roles and functions, intended to develop the “integrator/facilitator” role of Chief Risk Officer, will be discussed first with the Department of Peace Operations in the third quarter of 2024 and then with the heads of the peacekeeping operations. The objective is to assign an existing senior official in each peacekeeping operation within existing resources and to reflect those responsibilities in the revised enterprise risk management policy. In addition, the assignment of the Chief Risk Officer to an existing senior executive in each entity will be communicated through inter-office memorandums from the second line of defence entities and senior management of the Secretariat to all peacekeeping operations.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the ongoing review of enterprise risk management roles and functions, which is expected to be achieved by March 2025.

history.sg_progress: In all peacekeeping missions, senior-level staff are already overseeing enterprise risk management at a strategic level, often functioning as de facto chief risk officers. For instance, local risk management committees in peacekeeping missions are typically chaired by the Chief of Staff and/or the Chief of Mission Support. The outcomes of these meetings are often subsequently communicated to the mission’s senior leadership, including the special representatives and deputy special representatives of the Secretary-General, thereby ensuring alignment and informed decision-making. The Administration considers this recommendation to have been implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration assign the responsibility of Chief Risk Officer to an existing senior executive in each entity, at the department, missions and service centres levels.
history.administration_response: In line with United Nations enterprise risk management governance, the Administration confirms that senior- level officials provide strategic oversight of enterprise risk management at all peacekeeping operations. Noting that the United Nations does not have the Chief Risk Officer functional title in its human resources framework, these senior-level officials (normally Chief of Staff and/or the Chief of Mission Support) serve as Chief Risk Officer in their capacity as Chairs of local risk management committees. In line with the responsibilities of the Chief Risk Officer, the outcomes of the local risk management committee meetings are communicated regularly to the mission’s senior leadership, including the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and the Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, thereby ensuring informed, coordinated and risk-aware decision-making. Accordingly, the Administration respectfully requests the closure of the recommendation.
history.board_assessment: The Board acknowledges the progress made. However, the Administration previously mentioned that a review of enterprise risk management roles and functions was under way and scheduled for March 2025. Without a further update on this review, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.
